title: Design: Bulk deactivation confirmation looks as in the design
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create two active parts for this test, part A and part B.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Make sure no Cycle count is running on the Inventory list.
  • Make sure the app is in the Light theme.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1600 pixels wide with the page zoom at 100%, so the screen is as wide as the design boards.
  • Open the attached design picture of board 4.4 at 100% zoom, so you can compare the screen with it.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
  2. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  3. Click Deactivate parts.
  4. Click the part A row.
  5. Click the part B row.
  6. Click Deactivate on the dark bar.
  7. Click Cancel.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A and B are listed.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • The dark bar appears.

Step 4:

  • Part A is ticked.

Step 5:

  • Part B is ticked and the badge reads 2.

Step 6:

  • A white dialog with rounded corners opens in the middle of the page, and the page behind it, the dark bar included, is dimmed.
  • Its title "Deactivate parts?" is large and bold, with a thin line under the title row.
  • The lines read, in this order: "2 parts selected.", "These parts won't show up when adding parts to work orders, estimates, part sales or purchase orders.", "Existing records that use them stay as they are.", "Stock, cost of goods and QuickBooks aren't affected."
  • "Existing records that use them stay as they are." is a little bolder than the lines above it, and the "Stock, cost of goods …" line is grey.
  • A full-width box with the grey placeholder "Note (Optional)" sits under the lines.
  • A thin line runs above the footer; at the bottom right sit a white "Cancel" button with a grey outline, then a red "Deactivate" button.

Step 7:

  • The dialog closes, parts A and B are still ticked and the badge still reads 2: nothing changed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S10-R2: “The confirmation is the application's standard confirmation dialog. There is no confirmation word to type.”
  • S10-R3: “Raised from the bulk bar, the confirmation is titled "Deactivate parts?" or "Activate parts?". Raised from the part dialog, it is titled "Deactivate part?" or "Activate part?".”
  • S10-R4: “Raised from the bulk bar, the confirmation opens with "{n} parts selected.", or "1 part selected." for one. Raised from the part dialog, it opens with the part number followed by the description, as they stand in the form, with spaces before and after removed.”
  • S10-R5: “For a deactivation from the bulk bar, the confirmation then states, in this order: "These parts won't show up when adding parts to work orders, estimates, part sales or purchase orders.", "Existing records that use them stay as they are.", and "Stock, cost of goods and QuickBooks aren't affected." With exactly one part ticked, the lines read "This part won't show up ..." and "Existing records that use it stay as they are."”
  • S10-R9: “The "Existing records that use ..." line is medium weight. The "Stock, cost of goods and QuickBooks aren't affected." line is grey. Every other line is regular weight in the default text color.”
  • S10-R10: “The confirmation has a note field labelled "Note (Optional)". It stops accepting input at 255 characters.”
  • S10-R11: “The confirm button reads "Deactivate" in red for a deactivation and "Activate" in blue for a reactivation. Cancel sits to its left.”
  • S10-N1: “If the user cancels the confirmation, no part changes status.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "4.4 Confirm". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above where the PRD speaks, and from the board pictures where it is silent about the look.

The design also draws a grey close X at the right end of this confirmation's title row; the PRD lists only a title, a message, an optional note, Cancel and a confirm button. That difference is asked of Product (question Q8) and checked by the held design case "Design: Status confirmation has a close X in its title row"; this case follows the PRD and does not check the X.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • bulk-04-p4-4-confirm.png

The design's own words:

  • “"Deactivate parts?", "2 parts selected.", then the three lines of S10-R5 and the optional note. The Deactivate button is red (S10-R11).”
